'''Hamish Gordon Spencer''' {{post-nominals|country=NZL|FRSNZ}} is a New Zealand [[Evolutionary biology|evolutionary biologist]], and is a Distinguished Professor at the [[University of Otago]]. Spencer was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Society Te Apārangi]] in 2009, and is a Fellow of the [[International Science Council]]. He won the [[Paul Callaghan|Callaghan Medal]] in 2016.

==Academic career==

Spencer completed a [[PhD]] at [[Harvard University]] in 1988, under the supervision of [[Richard Lewontin]].<ref>{{Cite thesis|title= An investigation of the theories of speciation by founder effect
|last=Spencer|first=Hamish Gordon|type=PhD|publisher=Harvard University|url=http://id.lib.harvard.edu/alma/990018286140203941/catalog|date=1988}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Beyond Equilibria: Historical Approaches to Ecology and Evolution: Author information |url=https://global.oup.com/academic/product/beyond-equilibria-9780192858993?lang=en&cc=nz |access-date=2025-09-10 |website=Oxford University Press}}</ref> Spencer joined the faculty of the Department of Zoology at the University of Otago in 1992, rising to full professor in 2006.<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.otago.ac.nz/__data/assets/pdf_file/0023/295412/download-the-2007-calendar-472001.pdf |title=University of Otago Calendar |publisher=[[University of Otago]] |year=2007}}</ref> He was appointed one of seven University of Otago Sesquicentennial Distinguished Chairs in 2019.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Gibb |first=John |date=2019-10-01 |title=University's prestigious poutoko taiea initiative recognises leading scholars |url=https://www.odt.co.nz/news/dunedin/campus/university-of-otago/universitys-prestigious-poutoko-taiea-initiative-recognises |access-date=2025-06-27 |work=Otago Daily Times Online News |language=en}}</ref>

Spencer was director of the Allan Wilson [[Centre of Research Excellence]] for three years from 2012.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Hamish Spencer |url=https://council.science/profile/hamish-spencer/ |access-date=2025-06-27 |website=International Science Council |language=en-US}}</ref> He was an independent science advisor to the [[Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment]] for five years, beginning in 2016.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Hamish Spencer |url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/what-we-do/funds-and-opportunities/james-cook-research-fellowship/james-cook-research-fellowships-recipients/hamish-spencer/ |access-date=2025-06-29 |website=Royal Society Te Apārangi}}</ref> Spencer led the bid to hold the [[International Union of History and Philosophy of Science|International Congress of History of Science and Technology]] in New Zealand in 2025.<ref name=":0" />

Spencer is an evolutionary biologist, who uses mathematical models and genetics to explore the evolution and diversity of organisms, particularly New Zealand biota.<ref name=":3">{{Cite news |last=Fox |first=Rebecca |date=2015-02-11 |title=Old fossil 'tickled to death' at honour |url=https://www.odt.co.nz/news/dunedin/old-fossil-tickled-death-honour |access-date=2025-06-29 |work=Otago Daily Times Online News |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":2" /> He has worked on [[frequency-dependent selection]] and [[evolutionary developmental biology]], and is an expert on New Zealand's molluscan fauna.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /> He is also interested in the history of science, and has written about the [[history of eugenics]] and society's attitudes to [[cousin marriage]].<ref name=":1" /> Notable students of Spencer include [[Jemma Geoghegan]].<ref>{{Cite Q|Q111965714}}</ref>

==Honours and awards==
Spencer was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society Te Apārangi in 2009.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=View our current Fellows |url=https://www.royalsociety.org.nz/who-we-are/our-people/our-fellows/view-our-fellows/ |access-date=2025-06-27 |website=Royal Society Te Apārangi}}</ref> In 2016 he was awarded the Royal Society<nowiki>'s Callaghan Medal, for ''bringing ecological science into the marae and community''</nowiki>.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Gibb |first=John |date=2016-11-24 |title=Otago academics awarded national research medals |url=https://www.odt.co.nz/news/dunedin/otago-academics-awarded-national-research-medals |access-date=2025-06-27 |work=Otago Daily Times Online News |language=en}}</ref> In 2022 he was awarded a [[James Cook Research Fellowship]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=People |url=https://ssag.org.nz/people/ |access-date=2025-06-29 |website=Science System Advisory Group |language=en-NZ}}</ref> He has been a Fellow of the International Science Council since 2023.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Lewis |first=John |date=2024-01-25 |title=Honour to be ISC fellow: Otago evolutionary biologist |url=https://www.odt.co.nz/news/dunedin/campus/honour-be-isc-fellow-otago-evolutionary-biologist |access-date=2025-06-29 |work=Otago Daily Times Online News |language=en}}</ref>

The deepwater snail ''[[Hortia (gastropod)|Hortia spenceri]]'' is named after Spencer.<ref name=":2" />

== Personal life ==
Spencer is married to marine [[Biogeochemistry|biogeochemist]] [[Abigail Smith]].<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{cite web |date=2018 |title=Professor Abby Smith |url=https://www.sciencelearn.org.nz/resources/152-professor-abby-smith |website=Science Learning Hub}}</ref>
